covers: Weekend of 31 October–1 November 2026 and the Asian open on Monday 2 November (no US or JSE session since Friday's close)
headline: Oil drops more than 3% (Brent about $110) on hopes for the Qatari-led Iran talks; gold steadies near $3,900 and US futures are up about 0.4% into a week of midterms, Apple results and jobs data
summary: South Africa starts a short week: local government elections on Wednesday 4 November are a public holiday (BusinessTech), and the JSE's gold and PGM miners closed Friday 6–6.5% lower (LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct). In the US, S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 0.4% after last week's tech sell-off (Trading Economics via TradingView, 2 Nov), with Apple and Palantir reporting tonight, the midterms on Tuesday and the October jobs report on Friday 6 November (TradingKey, 2 Nov). Brent fell 3.3% to $109.70 early on Monday as Iran and Qatar held a third day of talks and Trump was reported to prefer more time for diplomacy (Investing.com, 2 Nov), and spot gold rose 0.6% to $3,900.05 after its worst October since 2008 (Investing.com, 2 Nov) — easier oil helps the rand and SA fuel-price outlook, but the US-Iran risk around Tuesday's vote remains.

items.title: Oil falls more than 3% on hopes for Qatari-led talks to end the Iran war; Brent $109.70
items.summary: By 05:27 GMT on Monday 2 November Brent January futures were down 3.3% at $109.70 a barrel and WTI down 3.5% at $100.48 (Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026), deepening an earlier 1.4% fall. Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araqchi called the talks with Qatar 'ongoing and progressing', and KCM Trade's Tim Waterer called the drop a 'technical pullback' after last week's gains, warning Brent could approach $120 if rhetoric escalates after Tuesday's US midterms (Reuters via Arab News, 2 Nov 2026). Citing an Axios report, Investing.com said Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu on Saturday he preferred to give diplomacy more time before deciding on renewed military action. OPEC+ kept December output targets unchanged. Cheaper oil helps the rand and SA fuel prices if it holds.
items.source: Investing.com; Reuters via Arab News, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: Earlier: oil fell 1.4% at the Asian open as Iran–Qatar talks ran into a third day
items.summary: At 00:11 GMT on Monday 2 November Brent was down $1.59 (1.40%) at $111.84 a barrel and WTI down $1.56 (1.50%) at $102.56, after Iranian and Qatari officials held a third straight day of talks on ending the war. Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran 'remained prepared for both defence and diplomacy'. Brent ended October at its highest level in six months, and the talks come amid concern that tensions could escalate after the US midterm elections on Tuesday (Angel One, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Rubio: the US would 'prefer to do it peacefully' with Iran; Trump 'hasn't made a decision' on new strikes
items.summary: At a press conference in Atlanta on Saturday 31 October, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said talks with Iran 'have actually never stopped', often through intermediaries, and that the president 'hasn't made a decision'. Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned the US and Israel not to restart strikes. Senator Chris Murphy alleged he had been briefed on a possible plan to resume attacks after Tuesday's vote. Reports say Qatari mediators are making progress on proposals that would let international inspectors into Iran in exchange for US sanctions relief (IBTimes, 31 Oct–1 Nov 2026).

items.title: Stock futures up about 0.4% after last week's tech sell-off
items.summary: Early on Monday S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 0.4% and Dow futures 0.3%. Last week the Nasdaq Composite fell 2%, the Dow 0.85% and the S&P 500 0.57%, after weak tech results and worries about AI spending (Trading Economics via TradingView, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Busy week: midterms Tuesday, October jobs report Friday, and Apple, Palantir, AMD and Qualcomm results
items.summary: Apple and Palantir report after the US close on Monday 2 November; AMD reports after the close on Tuesday 3 November, Qualcomm and Arm on Wednesday 4 November. ISM manufacturing is due Monday at 10:00 ET (16:00 SAST) and ISM services on Wednesday. The US midterm elections are on Tuesday 3 November, and the October employment report comes on Friday 6 November at 8:30 ET (14:30 SAST). The Fed's target range is 3.75%–4.00% (TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026). Reuters reported about an 80% chance of a December Fed hike (Tech Insider, Nov 2026).

items.title: Wednesday 4 November is a public holiday for the local government elections
items.summary: President Cyril Ramaphosa declared local government election day, 4 November, a public holiday under the Public Holidays Act by notice in the Government Gazette (BusinessTech). That makes this a four-day trading week for South Africa, with US results and the midterm outcome landing around the holiday.

items.title: Concor, the PIC-owned construction group, is in business rescue; more than 2,200 jobs at risk
items.summary: Concor's board found the business financially distressed and filed for business rescue on 6 October 2026, covering Concor Holdings, Concor (Pty) Ltd, Concor Construction and Concor Mining. The company is owned by the GEPF (81.25%) and UIF (18.75%), managed by the PIC, which cites liquidity and working-capital strain, legacy projects and guarantee calls after partner Murray & Roberts' 2024 rescue. Moneyweb reports more than 2,200 jobs at risk; Concor is a joint-venture partner on the R1.65 billion Msikaba bridge on the N2 Wild Coast road (Moneyweb, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Rand ended last week near R16.71, close to its weakest since July
items.summary: USD/ZAR closed Friday 30 October at 16.7075, up 0.59% on the day (rand weaker), trading 'near its lowest level since July' on a firmer dollar, weaker gold and PGM prices and high oil; over 12 months the rand is about 3.5% stronger (Trading Economics, updated 1 Nov 2026).

items.title: Gold back near $3,900 after its worst October since 2008; platinum still falling
items.summary: At 01:01 GMT on Monday spot gold was up 0.6% at $3,900.05 an ounce and silver up 1.4% at $49.83, while platinum was down 3.4% at $1,434.65 and palladium down 2.6% at $980.35. Gold had fallen 3.7% to a one-year low in the prior session. Lower oil eased some inflation worries; the US dollar index was down 0.2% at 101.88 (Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Goldman Sachs lifts its December Brent forecast to $105 from $90
items.summary: Goldman raised its December forecasts to $105 for Brent (from $90) and $94 for WTI, and its 2027 averages to $88 for Brent (from $80) and $78 for WTI (from $73), citing supply risks from the Middle East and Russia–Ukraine and adding a 1 million barrel-a-day disruption allowance to its 2027 base case (investingLive, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: AAPL and PLTR report tonight; both rated HOLD by the LRC Stock Scanner
items.summary: Apple (HOLD, score 61) closed Friday at $344.63, down 1.2%, and Palantir (HOLD, score 72) at $184.11, down 6.3% (LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026). Both report after the US close on Monday 2 November (TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026). Results can move the scanner score; ratings are not changed by this brief.
items.source: LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026; TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: AMD (Tuesday) and QCOM (Wednesday) report after Friday's chip sell-off
items.summary: AMD (HOLD, score 69) fell 10.9% to $504.80 on Friday and Qualcomm (HOLD, score 39) 11.1% to $164.79 in the Intel-led chip sell-off (LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026). AMD reports after the close on Tuesday 3 November and Qualcomm on Wednesday 4 November (TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026).
items.source: LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026; TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: JSE gold and PGM miners closed Friday 5.6–6.4% lower; gold's Monday bounce is a first test
items.summary: On Friday 30 October Gold Fields fell 6.4% to R553.06, Sibanye-Stillwater 6.4% to R35.77, Harmony 6.3% to R245.58, AngloGold Ashanti 6.0% to R1,340.52 and Implats 5.6% to R163.91, while Sasol rose 1.2% to R289.45 on higher oil (LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026). Spot gold's 0.6% rise in Asia (Investing.com, 2 Nov) is the first sign for Monday's open; platinum is still down.
items.source: LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026; Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026
